Council approves rail yard park after decade of debate

By Sam Rivera

The city council voted seven to two on Tuesday to convert the old rail yard into a public park, ending a decade of debate over one of the last large open parcels near downtown.

Under the plan, the first phase will open in 2028 and cost about $48 million, paid for mostly by a bond measure that voters approved in 2024. A second phase, which adds a community pool and playing fields, has no funding yet.

Supporters said the park would bring shade and green space to a neighborhood where summer temperatures run several degrees hotter than the city average. Opponents argued the land should have gone to housing, noting that the city is short roughly 12,000 homes by its own estimate.

Council member Dana Ortiz, who voted against the plan, said she was not opposed to parks but worried the city was choosing open space over people who need a place to live. "We can do both, but not on this parcel," she said.

The parks department expects to hire a design firm by spring. Residents will be able to comment on draft designs at three public meetings, the first of which is scheduled for March 12 at the Eastside Library.

Environmental testing found low levels of contamination from decades of rail use, which the city says will be capped under a layer of clean soil. State regulators signed off on the cleanup plan in October.
